= GitHub Workflows — what runs, and why some look duplicated

This directory holds the repo's CI/CD. A few workflows *look* like they overlap
but are deliberately distinct — documented here so the apparent duplication is
not "tidied away" into a real coverage gap.

== Hypatia runs in two places (on purpose)

* `hypatia-scan.yml` — the **standalone security scan** (push / PR / weekly).
  Independent; this is the repo's own Hypatia coverage.
* `static-analysis-gate.yml` -> `hypatia-scan` job — runs Hypatia as part of the
  **gate**, then the `deposit-findings` job hands the results to the
  **gitbot-fleet learning** pipeline. This job is also a *required status check*.

Same tool, two different consumers (security scan vs fleet learning). Removing
either loses real function — keep both.

== Secret scanning is single-sourced

`secret-scanner.yml` calls the standards reusable, which produces the three
required-but-independent contexts `scan / gitleaks` (working tree + full git
history + an AsciiDoc mirror pass), `scan / rust-secrets` and
`scan / shell-secrets`. An inline TruffleHog job was removed: the reusable
deliberately retired TruffleHog as redundant with gitleaks, so re-adding it was
duplicated work, not extra coverage.

Two rules for that caller, both learned the hard way:

* *Permissions.* The reusable's jobs declare `permissions: contents: read` and
  its own header says that is the whole requirement. A called workflow cannot
  exceed its caller's job-level grant, so an extra grant is spend without use;
  a missing one is a startup failure that produces ZERO jobs and no check run,
  which looks exactly like "the check never ran".
* *Suppressions.* A false positive in the scan is silenced by a fingerprint in
  the repo-root `.gitleaksignore` (`commit:path:rule:line`), not by widening a
  path or rule allowlist. Fingerprints do not blind future commits; allowlists
  do. See that file's header before adding an entry.

== SAST tools are complementary, not redundant

* `codeql.yml` — **retired 2026-09-29 (issue #52).** The advanced-config
  workflow could never go green while the repository has CodeQL *default
  setup* enabled: GitHub rejects its SARIF ("analyses from advanced
  configurations cannot be processed when the default setup is enabled",
  measured on run 35847705235). Default setup remains the repo's CodeQL
  pipeline; to restore workflow-based analysis, disable default setup in
  Settings → Code security first, then reintroduce this workflow.
* `sonarqube.yml` — SonarCloud (shell / JS surface; see `sonar-project.properties`).
* `static-analysis-gate.yml` — panic-attack + Hypatia gate (see above).

Each targets a different language/surface; together they cover what no single
analyser does.
